newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian milling wheat firms, barley drops limit.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian milling wheat firms, barley drops limit.

text.p: Hungarian milling wheat futures firmed on Thursday following comments from an agricultural organisation and a price rise in Chicago while feed barley futures eased on a very good crop outlook, traders said.

Milling wheat futures rose 110 forints and 130 forints per tonne for August and September respectively, to 19,970 and 20,060 forints. December firmed 290 to 21,000, while longer maturities rose by 290 to 400 forints in low turnover.
"Milling wheat rose partly because Chicago prices also rose by some one percent per bushel yesterday," said Janos Szolyka of Swap Ugynoki Kft.

"But also the National Alliance of Agricultural Producers (MOSZ) said that the crop will be by 500,000 tonnes below the expected five million tonnes, with lower quality due to lack of sunshine and weed control," he said.
He added some market players had reservations concerning the MOSZ comments which may have served to keep the price above 20,000 per tonne.
Feed barley prices continued yesterday's slump and closed down by the daily 400 forint limit for all contracts except August which lost 390.

The movement in feed barley futures except August will be freed on Friday and traders said barley was likely to see another limit fall as the six to seven tonnes per hectare yield forecast was outstanding.

August feed barley closed at 17,410 forints, December at 18,730 and March 1998 at 19,800. Producers cannot sell feed barley on the physical market above 17,000 forints, with the price moving between 16,000 to 17,000, traders said.
Volume on the Budapest Commodity Exchange's grains section was 715 lots (353 million forints), down from 1,122 lots (555 million forints) on Wednesday.
